blocks.content: The pattern of change in allele frequency shown in Figure 3.4 is very nearly that expected theoretically for an ideal population, as shown in Figure 3.5. This distribution was obtained by successive multiplication of a matrix whose elements are given by the transition probabilities in Equation 3.2. Although the full-blown theory of random genetic drift requires mathematics beyond the scope of this book (see Kimura 1955, 1964, 1976; Wright 1969; Crow and Kimura 1970; Kimura and Ohta 1971; Ewens 2004), in the next section we provide an introductory tidbit to impart the flavor. If you are a student with no background in calculus, the discussion may seem quite mysterious, but please do not be discouraged because a detailed understanding is not necessary to understand the rest of this chapter or anything later in the book.
